SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - SEPTEMBER 8, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.gov in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition,
verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

If the City Council adjourns to Closed Session, the City Council/Successor Agency will reconvene into Open Session after its conclusion and designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2025,
7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Rory Corrigan, Church in Cerritos.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Girl Scout Troop 135.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  Presentations

  A presentation was made by the City Council honoring:

  California’s 175th Anniversary of Statehood, received by Skye Connors, Southern
  California Regional Coordinator, Governor Newsom’s Office.

  Star Trek Day, received by The Fleet – A Star Trek Costuming Fan Group.

  Pastor Xiang Gao, Evangelical Formosan Church of Cerritos (Recognition of service to the
  City of Cerritos and the Highway 91 Region Vicinity Cities).

  5B.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to the Cerritos Advisory Boards
  (Boards, Commissions, and Committees) (2025-2027 term) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the
  public comments period closed.

  (minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 8, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 2 of 8

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to approve Mayor
  Yokoyama’s nomination listed below for a two-year term of service, through April 30,
  2027 (COUNCIL):

  Name  Advisory Board
  Brian Hews  Economic Development Commission

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

5C.  Review and consideration of the Mayor’s nominations for appointments to internal ad hoc
  working groups and external boards, commissions, and committees (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the
  public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Tse, to:

  1. Establish a new City Council Ad Hoc Working Group to serve as a liaison on matters
  related to the Bellflower Unified School District;

  2. Approve Mayor Yokoyama’s nominations for service appointments for his 2025-26
  Mayoral term, as listed below:

  City Council Internal Ad Hoc Working Groups
  Name  Liaisons
  Bellflower Unified School District  1. Yokoyama  2. Pulido
  ; and

  3. Direct the Office of the City Clerk to prepare and post a “City of Cerritos
  Appointments Brochure” to the City’s website, and to coordinate the dissemination of
  contact information to the respective appointees (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 8, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 3 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  David Pylman expressed concern regarding Closed Session Reports and offered
  suggestions for additional, agendized periods of public comment at public meetings.

  Sam Desai thanked the City Council for its recognition of Star Trek Day, encouraged
  additional public participation at the City’s Water and Sewer Rate Open House community
  meetings, and expressed concern regarding appointments to the City’s Advisory Boards.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, August 28, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Hong, to approve the Thursday,
  August 28, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated September 08, 2025 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Hong, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  September 8, 2025  $7,546,368.10 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 8, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 4 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.2. City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending June 30, 2025
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Hong, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending June 30, 2025
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.3. Approval of 2024-25 Q4 budget & audit compliance report (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Hong, to:

  1. Receive and file this report and its exhibits; and

  2. Ratify the executed Budget Amendments from the fourth quarter of Fiscal Year 2024-
  25 as detailed in the attached Budget Adjustment Log of the agenda report associated
  with this item (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of right-of-way use agreement with the Gateway Cities Council of Governments
  (GCCOG) for the installation, maintenance, and operation of the Gateway Cities Regional
  Fiber Optic Network (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Hong, to:

  1. Approve the Right-of-Way Use Agreement (Agreement) between the City of Cerritos
  and the Gateway Cities Council of Governments for the installation, maintenance, and
  operation of the Gateway Cities Regional Fiber Optic Network within City rights of-
  way;

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to administer the Agreement, including
  approval of finalized plans and related project actions; and

  3. Approve an exemption to the City's street cut moratorium for Bloomfield Avenue
  between Lucas Street/SR-91 Freeway Westbound Onramp and Alondra Boulevard,
  as required to meet state grant deadlines and facilitate timely completion of the
  Gateway Cities Regional Fiber Optic Network project (COUNCIL).

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 8, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 5 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Approval of an amendment to the agreement between the City of Lakewood and the City
  of Cerritos for reimbursement of Helicopter Patrol Services for the period of July 1, 2024
  through June 30, 2029 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Hong, to:

  1. Approve the Amendment to Agreement for Reimbursement for Helicopter Patrol
  Services from July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2029; and

  2. Authorize the Mayor to sign the Amendment to Agreement for Reimbursement for
  Helicopter Patrol Services (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

REORDERING OF THE AGENDA
At this juncture, the City Council, by consensus, reordered the agenda to consider New and Old
Business Item 9B prior to consideration of Item 9A.

9A.  Review and consideration of options related to Measure A funding compliance
  requirements (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, Director of Community and Cultural Services.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Joan Pylman expressed support for maintaining the City's current reservation and class
  policies, affording priority reservations and reduced class fees for Cerritos residents. She
  also expressed concern regarding the City’s facility reservation process, and requested
  the ability to make reservations for recreation facilities at various recreation facilities, or
  City Hall.

  David Pylman expressed concern regarding potential impacts to City facilities and
  programming, if City policies are not amended, resulting in a “Not in Good Standing” for
  Measure A status, for the City.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 8, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Hong, to direct staff to continue the
  City's current reservation (City Facility Use and Rental Policy, Policy No. 7.08) and class
  policies at Cerritos Park East and Liberty Park II, that provide priority reservations and
  reduced class fees for Cerritos residents, resulting in the City being "Not in Good
  Standing" for Measure A funding (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Johnson
  NOES:  Pulido, Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of consultant services for the provision of City of Cerritos
  Building and Safety services (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sabrina Chan, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Melissa Demirci, Transtech Engineers, Inc., expressed support for continued negotiations
  and contracting between the City and Transtech Engineers, for Building and Safety
  Services, and provided additional information regarding contract services offered.

  Jeff Goldenberg expressed concern regarding the existing level of service provided under
  the current Building and Safety Services contract with the County of Los Angeles.

  Jeff Stewart, Willdan Engineering, expressed support for continued negotiations and
  contracting between the City and Willdan Engineering, for Building and Safety Services,
  and provided additional information regarding contract services offered.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  ORIGINAL MOTION (HELD PENDING): It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by
  Pulido, with acceptance of a friendly amendment by Hong, to direct staff to:

  1. Invite the two (2) consulting firms presented to the City Council for consideration of
  award of contract, for RFP No. 1562-25, City of Cerritos Building and Safety Servies,
  to submit a final-and-best proposal: (Transtech Engineers, Inc. and Willdan
  Engineering, alphabetically listed); and

  2. Prepare an agenda report for City Council for review and consideration of the final
  proposals submitted at the scheduled 7:00 p.m., October 13, 2025 City Council/
  Successor Agency Special Meeting (COUNCIL).

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION (ADOPTED): It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Tse, to
  direct staff to continue to contract building and safety services to the County of Los
  Angeles (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 8, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Johnson
  NOES:  Pulido, Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal
  legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  Reports

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  Robert A. Lopez, City Manager, invited residents to participate in the City’s upcoming
  Community Open House event on Tuesday, September 9, 2025, related to consideration
  of water and sewer rate adjustments, at the Cerritos Senior Center.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Hong and Pulido, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and
  Mayor Yokoyama.

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to: 1. Identify several professional
  conferences for education and training of the City’s Planning Commission (PC) members;
  and 2. Provide the conference/training information to the PC, requiring members to
  attend at least one (1) training within the first year of their term.

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to: 1. Identify several professional
  conferences for education and training of the City’s Economic Development Commission
  (EDC) members; and 2. Provide the conference/training information to the EDC,
  requiring members to attend at least one (1) training within the first year of their term.

12.  Closed Session

  Pam Lee, City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session to
  discuss Item 12A, as listed on the Closed Session agenda.

  12A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - EXISTING LITIGATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) (COUNCIL)
  Name of Case: Castro v. City of Cerritos
  (U.S. Dist. Ct., Central Dist. Cal., Case No. 2:24-cv-09625-CBM-Ex)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 8, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 8 of 8

12.  Closed Session (continued)

  The City Council recessed into Closed Session.

  The City Council reconvened into Open Session.

  Pam Lee, City Attorney, provided the following Closed Session report:

  The City Council convened into Closed Session to discuss Item 12A. There was no
  reportable action taken and there was nothing further to report.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 11:38 p.m.
